status.en: 181 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 181 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat during an encounter in Kulgam, where he had taken shelter in a mosque and refused repeated calls to surrender. The operation also resulted in the recovery of a body and weapon, and linked a man who had previously sheltered the commander to the cell. In Manipur, over 1,000 CRPF personnel were redeployed from Chhattisgarh, including the withdrawal of an anti-Naxal battalion, while Maharashtra announced a Rs 1.5 lakh reward for information on looted weapons. The ISI revived a K‑2 plan to coordinate multiple terror groups for attacks in Punjab. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker drepte Lashkar-e-Taiba-kommandanten Lateef Bhat under et oppgjør i Kulgam, hvor han hadde søkt tilflukt i en moské og avviste gjentatte oppfordringer om å overgi seg. Operasjonen førte også til funn av en kropp og et våpen, og knyttet en mann som tidligere hadde gitt kommandanten husly til cellen. I Manipur ble over 1 000 CRPF-personell omplassert fra Chhattisgarh, inkludert tilbaketrekning av et anti-Naxal-bataljon, mens Maharashtra kunngjorde en belønning på Rs 1.5 lakh for informasjon om stjålne våpen. ISI gjenopptok en K‑2‑plan for å koordinere flere terrorgrupper i angrep i Punjab. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
